title: Build a Consent-First Customer Inquiry Workflow
rights: Original educational script and text graphics for RMC AI Workshop/APEX. Local synthetic CMU Flite narration. No third-party music, photos, clips or client data.
description: Original small-business tutorial showing how to capture inquiries with clear consent, limit data, use a human handoff, and test an automated acknowledgement with fictional customers. This is a demonstration, not legal advice or a live customer delivery system. Synthetic narration. No promised earnings.

scenes.heading: A lead form is not permission
scenes.text: Ask what follow-up the person wants.
scenes.narration: A visitor submitting a question is not blanket permission for every campaign. Design the form around the specific response requested, and record the permission you actually received.

scenes.heading: 1. Explain the purpose
scenes.narration: Tell visitors whether you will email a reply, call about a quote, or send a confirmation. Avoid hiding marketing enrollment inside a general contact form.

scenes.heading: 2. Keep only useful fields
scenes.narration: For a simple inquiry, ask only for information needed to respond. Never collect passwords or payment details through an ordinary contact form.

scenes.heading: 3. Record consent evidence
scenes.text: Consent choice plus time and form version.
scenes.narration: Store the selected permission, submission time, and the version of the notice. Keep access limited, and respect withdrawal and deletion requests.

scenes.heading: 4. Draft, don't auto-promise
scenes.narration: Your workflow can suggest an acknowledgement, but route pricing, complaints, emergencies, and unusual requests to a person. Never claim a service was delivered because a message was sent.

scenes.heading: 5. Test before real use
scenes.narration: Try a missing-consent submission, a duplicate inquiry, and an opt-out. Confirm each is handled correctly before activating anything for actual customers.

scenes.heading: Build trust before scale
scenes.text: Clear permission. Useful replies. Verified outcomes.
scenes.narration: A small, respectful workflow is easier to support and improve. Follow RMC AI Workshop for original tutorials on safer small-business automation.
